activity.title: Brush to the Song
activity.goal: Keep going at a task until a song ends: a song as a timer.
materials: Toothpaste, as much as your dentist or child health clinic advises
activity.safety: Everyone uses only their own toothbrush. Use as much toothpaste as your clinic advises. The child stands still while brushing: no walking or running with a brush in the mouth. If there is an accident, call your local emergency number.
activity.forAdult: In the story, Little Hippo brushes her top teeth and her bottom teeth side by side with Papa. This activity turns brushing into a song with a clear end: you brush while you sing, and you stop when the song stops. A song is a timer a toddler can hear. Sing the book’s refrain twice, to any tune you like: “Brush, brush, top teeth. Brush, brush, bottom teeth.” Stand side by side at a mirror, each with your own brush, and brush your own teeth as you sing, so the child can copy you. Then brush the child’s teeth too, as your clinic advises. To make it easier, sing it once, slowly. To make it harder, let the child lead the song. If the child does not want to open wide, play Little Hippo’s yawning game: who can open the widest?
activity.inClass: No shared brushes, and no real brushing at kindergarten. After washing hands, children sit in a circle of up to four with one adult and “brush” with a clean finger while everyone sings the song twice: top teeth first, then bottom teeth. Real brushing stays at home.
